title: Drishyam 3 Sells 4.05 Lakh Tickets in Advance, 7th-Biggest Pre-Sale Ever
excerpt: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion has sold around 4.05 lakh opening-day tickets in PVR Inox and Cinepolis, ranking 7th all-time and second in 2026, with trade forecasting a Rs. 50 crore opening on Gandhi Jayanti.
body:
• Drishyam: The Conclusion (Drishyam 3) sold around 4.05 lakh opening-day tickets across PVR Inox and Cinepolis — the 7th-biggest Bollywood advance sale ever, between War and Chennai Express.
  • It is the second-biggest pre-sale of 2026, behind only Dhurandhar 2, and has already beaten the final advance sales of Drishyam 2 across the national chains.
  • Trade forecasts peg the opening day at around Rs. 50 crore, with a chance of hitting Rs. 55 crore — which would make it Ajay Devgn's biggest opener and one of the year's biggest grossers.
  • The film releases on October 2, coinciding with the Gandhi Jayanti national holiday, giving it an extended opening window.

The finale of Ajay Devgn's beloved thriller franchise is roaring into cinemas. Drishyam: The Conclusion — the third chapter in the Drishyam series — has recorded the 7th-biggest advance sale in Bollywood history, selling around 4.05 lakh tickets for its opening day in the top two national multiplex chains, PVR Inox and Cinepolis, according to Pinkvilla.

That figure places it between War (4.10 lakh) and Chennai Express (4.00 lakh) on the all-time list, and makes it the second-biggest pre-sale of 2026, behind only Dhurandhar 2 at 8.75 lakh. Trade trackers note the film has already surpassed the final advance sales Drishyam 2 managed across the national chains — with booking still open — underscoring how much goodwill the franchise has built over a decade.

Starring Ajay Devgn, Tabu, Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj, and directed by Abhishek Pathak, the film is backed by Panorama Studios and Star Studios. It releases on October 2, the Gandhi Jayanti national holiday, a slot that hands it an extended opening window. As per Pinkvilla's forecast, the film is looking at an opening of Rs. 50 crore, with a chance of touching Rs. 55 crore if word-of-mouth catches fire.

Context & Background

The Drishyam franchise has been a rare sure-fire brand in Hindi cinema. Both earlier films — the 2015 original and the 2022 sequel — were modestly budgeted thrillers that over-delivered at the box office on the strength of tight screenwriting and Devgn's everyman hero Vijay Salgaonkar, a father whose fight to protect his family keeps colliding with the law.

The final chapter picks up that thread with a heavier cast: Tabu returns, and Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj add fresh dramatic weight. The advance numbers reflect a decade of audience trust converting into upfront sales — a pattern that has held for the brand even as the wider industry has struggled with inconsistent footfalls.

The broader tracking picture backs the excitement. Trade tracker Sacnilk's data showed around 4.77 lakh tickets sold across more than 21,000 shows over the first three days, with advance gross running into double-digit crores even excluding blocked seats — numbers that kept climbing through the final pre-release days.

Impact & Analysis

A Rs. 50-crore-plus opening would be the biggest of Ajay Devgn's career and one of the largest of 2026 — a meaningful marker in a year where the all-time advance chart has been reshuffled by huge franchise titles. Slotting into the 7th position ever, ahead of Chennai Express and close behind War, puts a mid-budget thriller franchise in company with the biggest star vehicles Bollywood has produced.

The real test comes after the first weekend. Pinkvilla and other trackers have been explicit: the trajectory now depends on word-of-mouth. The franchise's core strength — suspense-driven family drama — has historically played well with repeat audiences, and a positive reception could convert the record pre-sales into a sustained run through the holiday week.

Diaspora Angle

The Drishyam franchise has always traveled well with the Indian diaspora, and overseas screens in North America, the UK and the Middle East open alongside the Indian release. A record domestic opening would give diaspora audiences one more reason to catch Vijay Salgaonkar's final chapter in theaters rather than wait for streaming.

What's Next

All eyes are on the October 2 opening number and the weekend trend. If the film lands in the Rs. 50–55 crore band and holds through the Gandhi Jayanti holiday stretch, it would set up one of the biggest grossers of the year — and likely the biggest of Devgn's career. Actual collections, not advance trends, will settle the question.
